titre: The Hijri Calendar, or Why Ramadan Has No Fixed Season
accroche: In the year 10 of the Hijra, the Quran forbids resetting the lunar calendar to the seasons: Ramadan will cross them all, indefinitely.
contenu_vulgarise:
A Muslim who lives long enough will see Ramadan fall in the dead of winter, then in the height of summer, then pass through winter again, without any religious authority stepping in to reset it. This is not an oversight of the Muslim calendar: it is what it was designed for, since a decision made in the year 10 of the Hijra.

## A Calendar Deliberately Decoupled From the Sun

Before Islam, the Arab tribes of Mecca followed a lunar calendar, but a corrected one: an extra month, the nasī', was inserted from time to time so that the pilgrimage and the fairs that accompanied it would stay in the right commercial season. The decision rested with one family, the Qalammas of the Kinana tribe, who alone decided when to insert it, and therefore, in effect, the calendar of everyone. The Quran (sura 9, verses 36-37), revealed around the tenth year of the Hijra, at the Farewell Pilgrimage, breaks with this practice: it fixes the number of months at twelve and forbids any adjustment. Islam thus adopts a strictly lunar calendar, with no intercalary month at all: a religious and political break, since it takes away from one tribe the power to decide the common calendar alone.

The synodic lunar month lasts 29.53 days on average; twelve of these months make 354.36 days, against 365.24 for the solar year. The gap, close to eleven days each year, is never corrected: in a little over 32 years, Ramadan runs through all the seasons. It is only in the year 17 of the Hijra (638-639) that the caliph Umar formally instituted the Hijri era itself, counted from Muhammad's settling in Medina in 622, to date the caliphate's administrative correspondence, without touching the rule of twelve months set by the Quran.

## What This Shifts

Other religious traditions have solved exactly the same problem (making lunar months coincide with a solar year) by also inserting an extra month: the Hebrew calendar adds a thirteenth month seven years out of nineteen, according to what astronomers today call the Metonic cycle, so that Passover stays in spring. The Chinese calendar does the same so that the New Year stays in winter. Islam had this option at hand, it was the very practice it had just abolished, and it refused it on principle, not out of ignorance.

The result is therefore not a technical flaw: it is the lasting effect of a decision that, in the year 10 of the Hijra, aimed at nothing astronomical. It aimed to take away from one tribe the monopoly on the sacred calendar. Fourteen centuries later, that decision continues to produce its mechanical effect, with every new moon.

repere.texte: A synodic lunar month lasts 29.53 days on average; twelve lunar months make 354.36 days against 365.24 days for the solar year. The gap, close to eleven days a year, makes Ramadan run through all the seasons in a little over 32 years.

carte.punch: Ramadan has no fixed season. That is by design, since the year 10 of the Hijra.
carte.idee: The Muslim calendar is strictly lunar: it gains about eleven days on the seasons every year, and Ramadan crosses them all in 32 years. The Quran made this shift permanent by forbidding, as early as the year 10 of the Hijra, the corrective months of pre-Islamic Arabia.

quiz.question: Why does Ramadan never return to the same season from one year to the next?
choix: Because Islam adds a thirteenth month every two or three years, like the Hebrew calendar
Because the Hijri calendar is calculated on the solar year, like the Gregorian calendar
Because the twelve-month lunar year is about eleven days shorter than the solar year, with no correction at all
Because each caliph set a different starting date for Ramadan
quiz.explication: The 354-day lunar year gains eleven days each year on the 365-day solar year; unlike the Hebrew calendar, Islam in fact forbade this correction in the year 10 of the Hijra, and the Hijri calendar is not solar.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Before the Quranic prohibition, who decided on the insertion of the intercalary month nasī' in Arabia?
choix: The caliph Umar, starting in the year 17 of the Hijra
The family of the Qalammas, of the Kinana tribe
A council of tribes gathered every year in Mecca
The astronomers of Babylon, consulted by merchants
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The pre-Islamic nasī' was administered by the Qalammas of the Kinana tribe, who alone decided when to insert it; Umar intervenes only later to institute the Hijri era, without touching this rule.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How does the Hebrew calendar resolve the gap between lunar months and the solar year, unlike Islam?
choix: By simply abolishing lunar months in favor of the solar calendar
By keeping two parallel calendars, one civil and one religious
By inserting a thirteenth month in certain years, so that its festivals stay in the same season
By consulting a council of astronomers each year to set a new rule
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Hebrew calendar adds a thirteenth month seven years out of nineteen, according to the Metonic cycle, so that Passover stays in spring; Islam had this option, practiced in Arabia before it, and refused it in the year 10 of the Hijra.
